RESEARCH_QUESTION: Does forcing DEFEND onto exactly the one ACTIVE agent closest to its own flag at t=0 (state-dependent, fixed for the episode), on top of the frozen native pi_A rollout, create the desired A/B specialization separation against the frozen pi_B comparator -- mirroring the exact question and mechanism the 4v4 CLOSEST_DEFENDS_SCREEN_4V4 answered YES to (pattern_match=TRUE, SEALED 41575677) before any PPO training was attempted there?

IMPORTANT_PRIOR_RESULT_TO_WEIGH.what_it_found: The SAME install_forced_defend_target mechanism, on the SAME two 6v6 checkpoints, but with SEED-ROTATED defender-id selection (seed % 6, deliberately geometry-independent), found SCIENTIFIC_VERDICT=ONE_DEFENDER_HARM_ONLY: pi_A on Pole B resolved harm (delta -0.177 [-0.260,-0.104]), pi_B on Pole B resolved harm (delta -0.094 [-0.156,-0.042]); both Pole-A cells were unresolved (near zero, no significant effect either way). No cell resolved improvement anywhere.
IMPORTANT_PRIOR_RESULT_TO_WEIGH.why_this_screen_is_not_a_blind_repeat: The harm was concentrated specifically in the Pole-B cells for BOTH policies, and prior informal localization pointed to carrier-conversion disruption -- a seed-rotated defender id can land on an agent that is mid-attack or carrying the flag deep in enemy territory, which install_forced_defend_target then yanks back toward home regardless of game state. CLOSEST_DEFENDS selection is computed ONCE at t=0, before any carrying has occurred, on the agent already nearest its own flag -- the agent least likely to be mid-attack. This is the same reasoning that motivated running CLOSEST_DEFENDS_SCREEN_4V4 as a separate experiment from the seed-rotated scaffolded-A bridge at 4v4, where selection RULE was shown to matter (the closest-to-home screen matched/exceeded the seed-rotated bridge's own sealed numbers).
IMPORTANT_PRIOR_RESULT_TO_WEIGH.risk_flagged_not_dismissed: It remains possible that ANY single forced defender (regardless of selection rule) is harmful specifically against the Pole B opponent (OP7: enable_intercept, enable_mines, high threat_radius) for reasons unrelated to which agent is chosen. If this screen also shows Pole-B harm concentrated in A_closest, that is evidence the mechanism itself (not the seed-rotation artifact) is the problem, and the composite-hierarchy approach should be reconsidered for 6v6, not just re-tuned.

PATTERN_MATCH_DECISION_RULE.classification: DESCRIPTIVE / EXPLORATORY -- point estimates and bootstrap CIs are reported (n_boot=20000, alpha=0.05, rng_seed=7, matching every other record in this line) but this is not a confirmatory LCB95 gate. A pattern_match=TRUE result licenses training a real 6v6 pi_D (200k exploratory steps, 5A/1D, frozen pi_A on the other five slots) as the next PI-gated step, mirroring exactly how the 4v4 CLOSEST_DEFENDS screen preceded DEFEND_TEACHER/split-policy training there. It does not itself constitute a learned-crossover claim.

claim_boundary: Descriptive, exploratory comparison on the frozen, existing 6v6 learned specialists, fresh seeds, k=1 closest-to-home defender injection. Answers only whether this specific composite structure's win-rate pattern matches the desired A/B separation shape. Not a confirmatory claim, not a statement about whether a trained pi_D would do better or worse, and not a re-litigation of DEFENDER_INJECTION_CAUSAL_BRIDGE's already-sealed seed-rotated result (a different, disjoint experiment on the same mechanism).
